newsitem.title: CHINA: Foreign TV makers cut prices on China market.
newsitem.headline: Foreign TV makers cut prices on China market.

text.p: Several foreign colour television producers have slashed prices in China this year, triggering fierce competition with domestic makers, the Securities Daily said on Wednesday.
Prices of televisions made by Philips Electronics NV, LG Electronics INC and other foreign firms were about the same or lower than those of domestic competitors, it said.
Japanese firms have also put new products into the market, it said.

The excess production capacity of domestic producers coupled with competition from foreign manufacturers on price, technology and promotion has resulted in even stiffer competition this year than in 1996.
In recent years, about 10 large foreign colour television makers have set up in China, using the same sales channels as domestic makers and gaining from low labour costs, Securities Daily said.

Current sales of colour televisions were about 15 million a year while annual domestic production capacity was 36 million, the newspaper said, quoting figures from the Ministry of Electronics Industry.

Sichuan Changhong Electric Appliances Co Ltd, Shenzhen Konka Electronic (Group) Co Ltd and other domestic makers competed with foreign brands by cutting prices last year, raising market share to more than 70 percent, it said.
Foreign brands such as Panasonic, Sony Corp and Samsung Electronics Co Ltd were seriously hurt and their market share fell sharply last year, it said but gave no details.
